vulnerabilities.description: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability: innerHTML is used with unsanitized user-controlled content. The 'label' variable comes from DOM attributes and is concatenated directly into HTML without sanitization.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability: Second instance of innerHTML concatenation. While selected.length is safe, pattern demonstrates unsafe HTML construction that could be exploited if source changes.

Command Injection via graphviz: User-controlled dot file content is passed to execSync without validation. While stdin is safer than shell interpolation, malformed dot syntax could cause issues or be exploited.

Sensitive data stored in plaintext: Session context containing git branch, working directory, and user metrics stored in unencrypted JSON file at .claude-flow/sessions/current.json with no access controls.
No input validation on memory keys/values: Memory system accepts arbitrary data without validation, filtering, or encryption. Sensitive data stored as plaintext JSON.
Insecure WebSocket connection: WebSocket connects to window.location.host without explicit TLS validation. If page served over HTTP, connection vulnerable to MITM attacks.
No authentication on WebSocket: Events are sent without authentication tokens or origin verification. Any script can connect and send/receive events.
Predictable file locations: Memory and session data stored in predictable .claude-flow directories. Local file access could expose sensitive data.

recommendations: Replace innerHTML with textContent in helper.js (line 49, 54) or use proper DOM escaping/sanitization libraries (DOMPurify)
Validate and sanitize dot file content before passing to graphviz. Consider running graphviz in a sandboxed subprocess with resource limits
Encrypt session data at rest using Node.js crypto.createCipher() or similar; restrict file permissions to 0600
Add input validation and type checking to memory.js; implement encryption for stored values
Enforce HTTPS for WebSocket connections (wss:// protocol); add authentication tokens and origin validation
Implement access controls on .claude-flow directory; consider moving to OS-level secure storage (keychain/Credential Manager)
Add rate limiting to WebSocket event handlers
Implement logging and monitoring of security-sensitive operations (session creation, memory access, command execution)

summary.overallRisk: High - XSS and command injection vulnerabilities present; sensitive data stored unencrypted
